LESSON: KEEPING SAFE

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Home a) name various things found in the  Learners to identify and name 
Topic 2.1.3: Keeping safe

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Keeping safe. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. observe safety and security in the home 2.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: KEEPING SAFE
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Keeping safe helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: KEEPING SAFE
Study Keeping safe like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Observe safety and security in the home 2.

What this means
In this part you learn to observe safety and security in the home 2.. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe safety and security in the home 2..
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Keeping safe” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe safety and security in the home 2.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Keeping safe is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Keeping safe” around your school. (skill: observe safety and security in the home 2.)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Keeping safe to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: observe safety and security in the home 2..
3. Make one local Kenya example of Keeping safe from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Keeping safe: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Keeping safe?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Keeping safe means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: observe safety and security in the home 2..

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
